en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Twelfth Chapter
The Discourse on the Bad Destinations:
Is it the case that for a person endowed with right view, the bad destinations have been abandoned?
Yes, it is.
“Would a person possessed of right view feel lust for forms belonging to the states of woe?
“Yes.
“If a person possessed of right view would indeed feel lust for forms belonging to the states of woe, then surely it should not be said:”
“For a person endowed with right view, the miserable destinies have been abandoned.
Is it true that for a person endowed with right view, the miserable destinies have been abandoned?
Yes, it is.
A person endowed with right view [is not shaken] by sounds leading to states of deprivation … nor by odors … nor by tastes … [and so forth].

would he engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal, or a Naga maiden; would he accept goats and sheep; would he accept chickens and pigs; would he accept elephants, cattle, horses, and mares; ...
would he accept partridges, quails, peacocks, and pigeons?
“Yes.
“If that is so, and if a person accomplished in view were to accept a partridge, a quail, a peacock, or a francolin, then surely it should not be said:
‘For a person accomplished in view, the states of woe have been abandoned.’”
For a person endowed with right view, the lower realms have been abandoned; would such a person still take delight in forms leading to states of deprivation?
Yes. An Arhat has abandoned the lower realms; would an Arhat still take delight in forms leading to states of deprivation?
It should not be said thus ...

[and so on] ... for a person endowed with right view, bad destinations have been abandoned; a person endowed with right view [is free from] sounds ... odors ... belonging to the states of deprivation.

would he accept a partridge, a quail, a peacock, or a francolin?
“Yes,” you say.
“But has the Arahant abandoned rebirth in the miserable states? Would an Arahant accept a partridge, a quail, a peacock, or a francolin?
You must not say so… [and so on].
The states of woe have been abandoned by the Arahant; would the Arahant not be subject to passion for forms that lead to the states of woe? Yes.
Has the state of woe been abandoned by a person endowed with right view; would such a person endowed with right view not be subject to passion for forms that lead to the states of woe?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … for an Arahant,
a miserable rebirth has been abandoned, yet an Arahant does not [perceive] sounds pertaining to the states of woe … nor odors … [and so forth].
...in tastes ... in tangibles ...

he might engage in sexual intercourse with a non-human female, a female animal, or a Nāga maiden; he might accept goats and sheep; he might accept chickens and pigs; he might accept elephants, cows, mares, and she-asses ... [and so forth].
“Would one accept a partridge, a quail, a peacock, or a francolin?”— “Yes.
“But has a person endowed with right view abandoned rebirth in the miserable states, and would such a person not accept a partridge, a quail, a peacock, or a francolin?”— “No.”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“For a person endowed with right view, the miserable destinies have been abandoned”?
“Yes,” he said.
“A person possessed of right view might be reborn in hell … [or] might be reborn in the animal realm.”
"Would such a person be reborn in the realm of hungry ghosts?
"One must not say so.
"Therefore, it follows that for a person endowed with right view, the miserable destinies have been abandoned."
The Discourse on the Lower Realms is finished.
